title: Dental Tier Saving on an Annual Prepay Renewal — Premium Billing Accounts
content:
**Rule.** On a Cascade Individual Annual Prepay account of Premium Billing Accounts, a dental saving is deducted from the renewal payment when the renewal invoice bills the former tier of a departed dependent. The saving is deducted from the balance due; the total is floored at 0.00 and rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

| Departed dependent's termination date | Saving deducted |
|---|---|
| before the renewal start | the renewal invoice's months covered multiplied by the tier difference |
| inside the renewal year | the renewal year's months after the month of that date — its months covered less the whole calendar months from the renewal start to that date, less one — multiplied by the tier difference |
| any other case, or the renewal invoice does not bill the former tier | nothing |

Either saving is reduced by the prepay discount percentage (4 percent).

The renewal invoice is the invoice issued last (of two issued on the same day, the one recorded first); the renewal year is its coverage months, starting with its coverage month (the renewal start) and running for its months covered, and renewal premiums are reduced by the arrangement's prepay discount percentage (4 percent on Cascade Individual Annual Prepay). The departed dependent is the subscriber's child, spouse or domestic partner whose Dental PPO Plans enrollment funded by the account ended for loss of eligibility, the one with the latest termination date where more than one is on record (of two with the same date, a child's before a spouse's or domestic partner's, and of two of one relationship the one recorded first); the former tier is the coverage tier recorded on that enrollment. The subscriber's current dental tier and plan are those of the subscriber's active dental enrollment funded by the account with the latest coverage effective date (of two, the one recorded first). The tier difference is that plan's monthly premium for the former tier less its premium for the current tier, never less than zero, and zero where no departed dependent or no active subscriber enrollment is on record. The ended rider is the Orthodontic Benefit Riders rider funded by the account whose status is terminated, the one with the latest termination date (of two with the same date, the one recorded first); its premium is the rider plan's monthly premium per covered person.

**Reading the renewal invoice.** The renewal invoice is read against the plans it could bill: its premium is its months covered multiplied by the total of the monthly premiums of the plans priced, reduced by the prepay discount percentage and rounded half up to the cent. The plans priced are the subscriber's dental plan; each orthodontic rider the account funds that is active or applied, at its plan's monthly premium per covered person, riders applied for after the renewal invoice's date being left out; the subscriber's Prepaid Dental HMO Plans enrollment funded by the account that is applied or active (neither terminated nor cancelled) (the one with the latest coverage effective date, the one recorded first on a tie) at its recorded tier when it was applied for on or before the renewal invoice's date; and the subscriber's Vision Plans enrollment (the subscriber's vision enrollment funded by the account that is applied or active (neither terminated nor cancelled), the one with the latest coverage effective date, the one recorded first on a tie, priced at its plan's monthly premium for its recorded coverage tier) when it was applied for on or before the renewal invoice's date.
This reading is made only on an account on which, for each orthodontic rider plan, its active riders and, separately, its applied riders were either all applied for on or before the renewal invoice's date or all applied for on one date, so that the records show which riders were applied for after that date (when that one date is later, those riders).
The renewal invoice bills the former tier when its amount equals, to the cent, that premium with the dental plan priced at the former tier, with or without the ended rider priced in. On any other account than one where the reading is made, the renewal invoice is taken not to bill the former tier and no dental saving is deducted.

Whole calendar months from one date to a later one are counted the way an anniversary is counted: a month is complete only when a later month reaches the same day number, and the last day of a shorter month does not complete it.

**Hypothetical cases** (renewal start 1 October; renewal invoice for 12 months; tier difference 31.20; the invoice bills the former tier).
- Dependent's termination date 31 August: before the renewal start — 12 multiplied by 31.20, less 4 percent: 359.424, carried unrounded.
- Termination date 31 January: whole months from 1 October to 31 January are 3; 12 less 3 less one is 8 months; 8 multiplied by 31.20, less 4 percent: 239.616.
- Termination date 1 October of the following year: outside the renewal year — nothing.
